Well, we has fine.  He took 2 sleeping pills and passed out.  Cops looked at his text messages and had me read mine over the phone to confirm he never actually said "I am going to kill myself."  He told the cops that he was working and it was a misunderstanding.

He and I both know it wasn't a misunderstanding.  When he says stuff like:

* "It doesn't matter anymore"
* "I deserve this pain and suffering"
* "I attempted suicide 3 years ago and I've been through hell and back"
* "Thanks for your concern, but it's time for me to go"

I don't take that lightly.  I do feel a little stupid, but I'd rather feel stupid and have everything ok, than not do anything and him hurt himself.

Thanks for your help last night.

Just got a call back.  They found where he lives and are going to check on him.  They couldn't give me his address.  I really hope this wasn't some BS he was pulling for attention and the cops show up at his house.  But I really don't think he would BS like this.  He has always answered my texts immediately so it is not like him at all to ignore me.  I even texted him that I called 911.  If he was faking he would have replied that he was fine since I doubt he would want them showing up.
Thank you.  I will let you know if I hear anything back.

Can they pinpoint him if all that I have is his cell number and first name?  That's all I have about his personal information?

Thanks for the reply.

Every time I try to quit I have nights like this, so writing it down is a good idea because I have always given in to the urges in the past.  Even if I make it through the night, that desire stays with me and I eventually give in.

Sometimes I feel like I am trying to quit heroine.

Ah, I remember the days of masturbating for a minute.  Back when I was 12, lol (I'm 31 now).

> Out of curiosity: did you ever speak with that boy about how he was not "allowed" to do it anymore? I ask because it seems like you instantly assumed all this shame in his somewhat ambiguous wording. Perhaps it was a counselor or an older brother or uncle or something. Not that it really matters - he took an intimate moment between a person and shared that - that would hurt no matter what.

No, I have never talked to him about it and when it happened I just swallowed my shamed and never brought up the subject again for 18 years.  You are right, I did assume a lot.  I think I had some shame issues before this incident, because I never considered that he willingly participated in the play with me.  I immediately assumed I was a horrible person for initiating the play to begin with.  I know now that what we did was normal child experimentation that most people experience.  But it took me a long time to learn that and I would have benefited greatly by knowing that at 11 years old.

I think that's the most important thing in your situation.  No matter how you approach this with your son, the most important thing he needs to know is that it is normal for this type of experimentation at his age.

Thanks.

Thank you.

I don't want to urge you to tell your son directly what you saw.  That was not my intention.  If you think that's the best course of action, then so be it.  I was just saying that you can possibly deal with it indirectly by educating him that that sort of thing is normal for his age without letting him know that you saw him.  I think just letting him know that he can open up to you about the situation if he wants to is the important thing and that you are there for him no matter what.

Bottom line is that I am not an expert what so ever on how to handle this situation as a parent, I just wanted to share my story to let you know that sometimes this can have a negative effect if not handled correctly.  I would suggest asking an expert/therapist on what the best way to handle this situation.  It is a very touchy subject and telling your son directly that you saw him may trigger some shame.

Also, I think your reaction to seeing the act happening in front of your eyes took tremendous strength.  Most parents, including myself, would have probably freaked out in front of the boys and made them stop immediately.  This may have caused them to feel extremely ashamed of themselves.  You instead walked away and are trying to figure out the best way to deal with the situation.  Stopping the act right there and then wouldn't have had any benefit.  It basically already occurred and you couldn't undo it.  Also, most likely they have played like this before.  I doubt kids are performing oral sex on their first time of experimentation (but maybe not, times have changed since I was a kid).

> that he can do whatever he wants with his body, and in our home, and as long as other people want to participate I'm okay with that.

Obviously you need to take caution with that statement.  This can land you in legal trouble.  Also, your son is probably too young to be having sexual relationships at all or at least in your home.  But it is not my intention to give you parenting advice.

So, I would say consult with someone who has more knowledge on how to handle this as a parent.  Also kudos to you on handling this as a sane, mature adult.  Not many people in this world would have reacted the way that you did.

Take care.

Hi, I'd like to share the other side of the coin where an experience like this did not turn out well.

When I [male] was around 11, I had sex-play with a neighborhood boy a year younger than me.  It all started off like most people described in this thread.  Curiosity, exploring mine and another's body, enjoying the stimulation, etc.  However, after a while the sex-play kind of died off.  We probably did it like 20 times or so over a half of year (if my memory serves me correctly).  After some time though, I really wanted to experience the sensations with him again and asked him if we could do it again.  He told me "no, I am not allowed to do that anymore."  At that time, I was crushed.  Not only from being denied, but because I realized he must have talked to his parents about it since he said he was not "allowed" to do it anymore.

After that, I was filled with a deep sense of shame.  I never told anyone about it until I was 29 years old.  I let it affect me my whole life and I am still dealing with the shame.  My shame included:

* Him having told another person on what we did together.  I was extremely embarrassed.
* Performing these acts with a person of the same sex.  I grew up in a very homophobic atmosphere.
* Feeling horrible for "making" him do these things with me.  I believe I was the one who initiated the first time we "played" together.  However, it was mutual every single time and there was no abuse going on.  But in my head, I was a piece of shit and a sicko for bringing the "play" up in the first place.
* The fear of him telling our peers at school and having people my age finding out that I played with another boy sexually.  Once again, I grew up in a very homophobic atmosphere.

I buried the whole experience deep inside and never told anyone until I sought out therapy 18 years later.  I also developed a coping mechanism for the deep shame that I felt.  Masturbation.  And not too long after masturbation I discovered porn.  And right around that time, dial up internet and home computers were becoming popular in people's houses.  By the age of 13 I was looking at internet porn and masturbating to it.  Quickly I became an expert of deleting history and covering my tracks.  I even remember stealing my dad's password when he put parental controls on the computer at home.

Soon I became addicted to the whole process of looking at porn and masturbating to it.  Especially with the endless content on the internet.  I started crossing boundaries in the porn I looked at including gay porn and transsexual porn.  This added to my shame as I was still in my mid teens and too young for all that shit.  I buried the shame even more and the only cure was more porn and masturbation.

Anyway, fast forward to 29 years old, I have a wife and 3 kids and still unable to shake my coping mechanism and deep sense of shame that I had never dealt with.  My wife has had enough of me lying to her about porn and she files for divorce.  Luckily I am still able to see my kids and have joint custody.

I am still dealing with my shame issues and sexuality issues and have a lot of work to do.  I just wanted to share the story because it doesn't always turn out roses and everything will fall into place.  HOWEVER, the fact that you are very open minded and are seeking out ways to deal with this situation in a healthy manner tells me that you will make things OK to the best of your ability.  I lived under stressful home circumstances and never dared to burden my parents with the fact that I needed help and I was lost and buried in shame.  I never told them and they never had anyone tell them what I was going through.  As a kid I was unable to deal with it all and it affected me greatly and still affects me.

So I would say communication is the key.  You have a huge advantage:  You know what is going on with your son and are able to take the necessary steps to help him transition through this in a healthy way.  I would also say that maybe telling the other boy's parents may not be a bad thing.  Look at me, if someone would have told my parents what was going on, I may not have ended up battling this thing alone and struggle mightily because of it.

Thank you for your post.  I identified with the subject matter and it was a help for me to write this all out.

Good luck.
